key_impacts: Nuclear fuel in Fukushima Daiichi reactors melted due to the accident
Ongoing cooling is required to avoid further release of radioactive materials; the accident continues
Coolant water becomes extremely contaminated and leaks into reactor building basements
About 400 tons of groundwater flow in daily, filling the site with many 1,000-ton tanks of contaminated water
Residents continue to bear serious impacts; rebuilding daily lives and communities is essential
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO's Fukushima Daiichi, directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
The accident is not over; operators circulate coolant to cool nuclear fuel that melted inside reactors to prevent further radioactive release.
Coolant becomes extremely contaminated and leaks into basements; 400 tons of groundwater flow in daily; the site is packed with 1,000-ton tanks.
missing_information: Directly affected settlements beyond the facility are not specified
Exact end date or full accident timeline not provided
